description: Create a GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow that automatically compiles the project on Windows using MSVC + vcpkg and publishes a release artifact (ZIP) containing the DLL, config, dictionaries, and tessdata. Also create the installer, uninstaller, and user documentation.
steps: Create .github/workflows/build-release.yml - a GitHub Actions workflow that: (a) triggers on push of a version tag (v*), (b) uses windows-latest runner, (c) sets up vcpkg from github.com/microsoft/vcpkg, (d) runs cmake --preset windows-msvc, (e) builds with cmake --build build/windows-msvc --config Release, (f) downloads eng.traineddata from https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata_best/raw/main/eng.traineddata, (g) packages build output into a release ZIP (bronco-v{version}-win64.zip) with structure: d3d11.dll, config/bronco_config.json, data/dictionaries/pt-br/*.json, data/tessdata/eng.traineddata, install.ps1, uninstall.ps1, README_INSTALL.md, (h) creates a GitHub Release with the ZIP attached using softprops/action-gh-release or similar

Create scripts/install.ps1 - a PowerShell installer script (must work with PowerShell 5.1+ on Windows 10/11) that: (a) displays a welcome banner for Bronco, (b) checks if running as Administrator (optional, warns if not), (c) auto-detects GW2 install folder by checking common paths (C:\Program Files\Guild Wars 2, C:\Program Files (x86)\Guild Wars 2, and registry key HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ArenaNet\Guild Wars 2 or similar), (d) lets user confirm or browse/type a custom path, (e) lets user pick target language from available dictionaries (list subdirectories under data/dictionaries/ in the extracted ZIP, default pt-br), (f) copies d3d11.dll to the GW2 folder, (g) copies config/ directory to GW2 folder, (h) copies data/ directory (dictionaries + tessdata) to GW2 folder, (i) updates config/bronco_config.json with chosen target_locale, (j) shows a success message with instructions to launch GW2, (k) handles errors gracefully with user-friendly messages

Create scripts/uninstall.ps1 - a PowerShell uninstaller script that: (a) auto-detects GW2 folder same as installer, (b) lets user confirm the path, (c) removes d3d11.dll from GW2 folder (with confirmation prompt), (d) removes config/ and data/ directories that Bronco created (preserving any non-Bronco files), (e) shows success message

Create docs/INSTALL.md (in Portuguese BR) - end-user installation documentation that explains: (a) how to download the latest release from GitHub Releases page, (b) how to extract the ZIP, (c) how to run install.ps1 (right-click > Run with PowerShell, or powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1), (d) how to uninstall, (e) how to change language after installation, (f) troubleshooting section (common issues: ExecutionPolicy, wrong GW2 path, antivirus false positive for DLL injection)

Update README.md to add a simplified 'Quick Install' section at the top of the installation instructions that points to the GitHub Releases page and describes the one-command install process, keeping the existing manual build instructions below it
acceptance_criteria: The GitHub Actions workflow YAML is valid and defines a complete CI pipeline triggered on version tags
The workflow packages all required files (DLL, config, dictionaries, tessdata, installer scripts) into a release ZIP
install.ps1 is a valid PowerShell script that auto-detects GW2 path, handles user input, copies files, and updates config
uninstall.ps1 is a valid PowerShell script that removes Bronco files from GW2 folder
docs/INSTALL.md provides clear step-by-step instructions for non-technical users in Portuguese BR
README.md has a new Quick Install section directing users to GitHub Releases
All scripts handle edge cases: GW2 not found, user cancellation, file copy failures
The install script lets the user pick their target language from available options
verification: Run 'python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\'.github/workflows/build-release.yml\'))"' to validate YAML syntax
Run 'pwsh -Command "Get-Content scripts/install.ps1 | Out-Null"' or equivalent PowerShell syntax check to validate the script
Run 'pwsh -Command "Get-Content scripts/uninstall.ps1 | Out-Null"' or equivalent syntax check
Verify the ZIP structure in the workflow matches the expected layout by reading the packaging step
Confirm all file paths referenced in scripts match the actual project structure (config/bronco_config.json, data/dictionaries/, data/tessdata/)
findings: All files created successfully. YAML validated with PyYAML (note: 'on' key parsed as boolean True which is expected PyYAML behavior but valid for GitHub Actions). PowerShell scripts validated for balanced braces/parens. pwsh not available on Linux sandbox so full PS syntax validation skipped. All file paths in workflow and scripts verified against actual project structure.
